newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds consolidate, seen in tight range.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds consolidate, seen in tight range.

text.p: German Bunds were little changed in late trading on Monday after a directionless day weighed upon by the market holiday in the U.S.
Bund futures were down seven basis points at 103.58 in late afternoon dealings, after trading between 103.39 and 103.64 throughout the day.

Dealers predicted that the market would remain rangebound until U.S. markets reopen in the European afternoon Tuesday, and was unlikely to be sparked into action by domestic money supply data due later this week or by the Bundesbank's regular policy-making meeting on Thursday.
"M3 (money supply) and the central bank council meeting are not really much of an issue," said one dealer.
"The January M3 number is always very volatile and the Bundesbank won't do anything on Thursday because of the situation with currencies," he added.
In the cash market, dealers noted that the long end was most in demand as investors tended to seek higher yields and accept increased risk.
The yield on the benchmark 10-year Bund was unchanged at 5.50 percent in late dealings, while the five-year Series 120 Bobl yielded 4.30 percent, just up from 4.29 percent.
The Bundesbank's announcement of plans to top up its Series 121 Bobl issue by 10 billion marks rather than the eight billion expected had weighed slightly on five-year issues, dealers said.
